To prove that the category of modules over a ring `ModuleCat R` has finite biproducts, we can leverage the fact that this category is additive. In an additive category, finite biproducts exist if and only if the category has finite products and finite coproducts, and the product and coproduct functors coincide (i.e., they are biproducts).

Since `ModuleCat R` is known to have finite limits and finite colimits (from the relevant Mathlib lemmas), and it is also additive (as it is a category of modules over a ring), we can conclude that it has finite biproducts. Specifically, the biproduct of a finite collection of modules is their direct sum, which exists in the category of modules. Therefore, the theorem follows from the general result that additive categories with finite products and coproducts have finite biproducts.
